title: Holeshot HUD — settings composition
question: Same tabs, same controls, same copy. Pick the composition the 800×700 settings window should be built to. What should carry forward? What feels false to Broadcast Booth Glass?

options.label: Show Plaque
options.thesis: The Show on overlay control is a full-width TV plaque — first-run cannot miss it; depth lives quietly underneath.
options.viewport: Left widget rail; Standings pane opens on a tall Holeshot-orange Show on overlay plaque with a large toggle; remaining controls (font, highlight, columns, snap) stack below in quieter charcoal.
options.risk: The plaque can steal so much height that mid-session column editing feels buried.

options.label: Header Strip
options.thesis: A persistent top strip holds the widget name and Show toggle — one glance, then the pane is all depth.
options.viewport: Holeshot mark + Standings + Show on overlay live in a window-wide header; left rail is compact names and on-dots; the body is the current controls at working density.
options.risk: A header chrome band can read as generic app toolbar if the orange plaque energy is too thin.

options.label: Pit Board
options.thesis: Settings as a classification board: tight rows, uppercase labels, orange only on the live switch and the selected rail.
options.viewport: Narrow rail like a P/# column; pane is a standings-like stack of control rows; Show on overlay is the first row — orange-filled when off, quiet when on.
options.risk: Too close to the HUD table and too dense for a 700px settings window.
